directAnswer: 2.4 GHz WiFi has better range because its lower frequency allows it to penetrate walls and obstacles more effectively than higher frequencies like 5 GHz.
summary: Understanding the range advantages of 2.4 GHz WiFi can help users optimize their home networks for better connectivity.

sections.heading: Frequency Penetration
sections.body: The 2.4 GHz frequency can travel further and penetrate solid objects like walls and floors better than 5 GHz, which is more susceptible to interference and attenuation.

sections.heading: Obstacle Interference
sections.body: 2.4 GHz signals are less affected by physical barriers compared to 5 GHz signals, making them more reliable in environments with many obstacles.

sections.heading: Device Compatibility
sections.body: Many older devices only support 2.4 GHz, ensuring broader compatibility for users with a mix of devices.

steps.title: Check WiFi Settings
steps.detail: Access your router's settings through a web browser by entering the router's IP address. Look for the wireless settings to confirm the frequency band.

steps.title: Switch to 2.4 GHz
steps.detail: If your router supports dual-band, select the 2.4 GHz band in the settings to improve range in areas with weak signals.

steps.title: Optimize Placement
steps.detail: Position your router in a central location to maximize coverage and minimize obstacles between the router and connected devices.

faqs.question: Can I use both 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz simultaneously?
faqs.answer: Yes, many dual-band routers allow you to use both frequencies at the same time, providing flexibility for different devices and uses.

faqs.question: What are the downsides of using 2.4 GHz?
faqs.answer: While 2.4 GHz offers better range, it is more prone to interference from other devices like microwaves and Bluetooth, which can affect performance.

faqs.question: How can I improve my 2.4 GHz WiFi signal?
faqs.answer: You can improve your 2.4 GHz signal by reducing interference, repositioning your router, or using WiFi extenders to boost coverage.

caveats: While 2.4 GHz has better range, it typically offers lower speeds compared to 5 GHz, which may affect performance in high-bandwidth activities.
